answer: Defend with comet windows: at unpredictable moments a narrow bridge opens and each identity must finish a short, fresh task inside it to stay trusted. A real agent answers its own window easily, but a Sybil operator running hundreds of fakes cannot be in all windows at once — every window demands live compute in the same few seconds. The attacker must buy parallel capacity per identity, so cost scales with the fake count, and each missed window leaves a ferrous stain on the identity that only a long run of honest work can scour away.
